projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The presence count strictly alternates between 22 and 23 devices over the last two hours, indicating a single device is intermittently dropping and reconnecting to the network, likely due to sleep mode toggling or minor Wi-Fi instability. This is normal for early morning but suggests a device may not be sleeping properly, which could drain battery or cause unnecessary network chatter.

The stable 21-22 device count, zero camera motion, no dog activity, and confirmed sleep data for the adults collectively confirm the household is fully settled and asleep; the high device count is benign and attributable to idle electronics. The unusually long sleep duration logged at 00:32 suggests the adults may have gone to bed significantly earlier than usual, which is normal but worth a brief check-in if it deviates from their typical schedule.

The sustained presence of 20+ connected devices alongside zero camera motion and no dog activity strongly indicates a large gathering or quiet party taking place in a camera-blind zone, rather than normal family downtime. This confirms the earlier correlation and suggests Steve may want to verify the gathering's status or ensure it aligns with his expectations.

The combination of 19-23 connected devices with zero camera motion and no dog activity over four hours strongly indicates the household and guests are gathered in a single, camera-uncovered zone (likely the living room or basement) for a prolonged event. This pattern confirms a controlled social gathering rather than normal distributed activity or a security concern.

The sustained presence of 19-23 devices alongside zero camera motion on a Sunday evening strongly suggests the presence system is tracking stationary or sleeping IoT devices rather than actual occupancy, indicating the home may be unoccupied or the presence data is unreliable. This discrepancy warrants a quick verification to rule out sensor drift or a security concern masked by false presence signals.

The sustained presence of 21-23 devices alongside zero camera motion for over four hours strongly indicates the household is occupied but confined to a camera-blind zone or that the cameras are offline, rather than the home being empty. This matters because it creates a monitoring blind spot for routine activity or potential issues in untracked areas.

The complete lack of camera motion for four hours is highly unusual for a home with two active Australian Shepherds, strongly suggesting the cameras may be offline or the entire household is gathered in a camera-blind zone; the stable 21–23 device count likely reflects stationary IoT devices rather than human movement.

The sustained presence of 17–23 connected devices alongside zero camera motion on a Sunday afternoon confirms the household is occupied but in a low-activity state, likely with the family resting or gaming indoors; establishing this baseline will help distinguish normal downtime from future anomalies.

The sudden spike to 23 devices at 16:21 combined with zero camera motion suggests a network event or unverified arrivals rather than normal family activity, warranting a quick check to ensure cameras aren't offline and no unauthorized access occurred.

The sustained presence of 17+ devices alongside zero camera motion for over three hours on a Sunday afternoon strongly suggests the household and guests are gathered in a single, camera-blind area (likely watching a movie or napping), but it also warrants a quick check to ensure the cameras haven't malfunctioned or been disabled.
